Note that this tool is not intended for describing, creating, deleting, or removing modes or routines. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The command must be specified as a string in Korean, consisting of the room name, appliance name (or alias), and operation command, separated by commas. **Sikhae (식해)** A Korean “raw‑fish salad” that’s spicy, tangy, and served cold. It’s a popular side dish (반찬) or appetizer, especially during the summer when you want something light and refreshing. --- ## Ingredients | Category | Item | Quantity | |----------|------|----------| | **Fish & Seafood** | Fresh raw fish (mackerel, sardine, pollock, or a mix) | 300 g | | | Shrimp (optional) | 100 g | | | Squid (optional) | 50 g | | **Vegetables** | Cucumber | ½ medium | | | Red onion | ¼ medium | | | Scallions (green onions) | 2 stalks | | | Sesame seeds | 1 tsp | | **Sauce** | Korean red pepper flakes (gochugaru) | 1 tsp | | | Korean chili paste (gochujang) | 1 tsp | | | Soy sauce | 1 tsp | | | Rice vinegar | 1 tsp | | | Sugar | ½ tsp | | | Sesame oil | ½ tsp | | | Garlic (minced) | ½ tsp | | | Salt | pinch | | | Black pepper | pinch | | **Optional** | Kimchi (thinly sliced) | 1 tbsp | | | Toasted sesame oil (for drizzling) | 1 tsp | > **Tip:** Use only the freshest fish you can find. If you’re unsure, ask your fishmonger to cut it into thin slices for you. --- ## Equipment - Sharp knife - Cutting board - Mixing bowl - Small spoon or chopsticks - Serving bowl or plate --- ## Step‑by‑Step Instructions | Step | Action | |------|--------| | **1. Prepare the fish** | • Rinse the fish under cold water.
• Pat dry with paper towels.
• Slice into bite‑size pieces (about 1 cm thick).
• If using shrimp or squid, clean and slice them similarly. | | **2. Chop the vegetables** | • Slice cucumber into thin half‑rings.
• Thinly slice the red onion.
• Chop scallions into 1‑inch pieces. | | **3. Make the sauce** | In a small bowl, whisk together:
• Gochugaru, gochujang, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, sesame oil, minced garlic, salt, and pepper.
• Adjust seasoning: more vinegar for tang, more sugar for sweetness, more gochugaru for heat. | | **4. Combine** | • Place all fish, shrimp, squid, cucumber, onion, scallions, and optional kimchi into a larger bowl.
• Pour the sauce over the mixture.
• Toss gently until everything is evenly coated. | | **5. Chill** | • Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a lid.
• Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (up to 2 hours) to let flavors meld. | | **6. Serve** | • Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds on top.
• Drizzle a little toasted sesame oil if desired.
• Serve cold, either as a side dish or with steamed rice. | --- ## Variations & Tips | Variation | How to Adapt | |-----------|--------------| | **Sikhae with only fish** | Omit shrimp/squid and kimchi. | | **Sikhae with more heat** | Add extra gochugaru or a splash of hot sauce. | | **Sikhae with a citrus twist** | Replace rice vinegar with lemon or lime juice. | | **Sikhae for a vegan version** | Use tofu or tempeh instead of fish; keep the sauce vegetarian. | | **Storage** | Keep refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 24 hours. | | **Safety** | If you’re not comfortable eating raw fish, you can lightly sear the fish pieces before adding them to the sauce. | --- ### Quick Reference - **Total prep time:** ~15 min (plus chilling) - **Total cook time:** 0 min (no cooking required) - **Serves:** 2–3 people Enjoy your homemade sikhae! It’s perfect for a quick, flavorful meal or as a party side.
